Build the QC object from the counts as delivered (no pre-normalization before the transform); attach metadata.

PCA on the 500 most variable genes (n_top_genes = 500)
Heatmap of Euclidean distances between samples

steps.name: DESeq2 Wald test, treated vs control, adjusted for sex and age
caveats: Length offset lost (Salmon import state unknown): state this explicitly wherever the results are summarized — changes in isoform usage can show as differential expression
Check whether the delivered values are integer; DESeq2 accepts non-integer Salmon estimated counts, but note the value type in the report
6 replicates per group: DESeq2 flags count outliers by Cook's distance and sets the p-value to NA in such cells rather than replacing counts; report how many genes this affects
steps.context: Import /eval-four-models-v2-with-variance-partition-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv as a gene-level count table as delivered. The import state is not established: the profile does not state whether Salmon length correction occurred, and no per-sample quantification files or average transcript length table are provided. Per the procedure, fit the count model on the counts as delivered with NO length offset, and state in the report that the length offset is lost and that changes in isoform usage can surface as differential expression. Do NOT run tximport on this gene table (tximport imports transcript estimates) and do not invent a length input. Pre-filter before the model; design ~ sex + age + condition; single contrast, condition treated over control.
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated and control, with sex and age held as covariates?

grounding.reason: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm log fold change shrinkage per R-0029@22ca

constraints: filter_low_counts: keep genes with at least min_count = 10 in at least min_samples = 6 samples (the smallest group size); the results-step independent filtering does the rest (filter_policy = minimal_then_independent)
normalize: median-of-ratios size factors estimated inside DESeq2; do not scale, transform, or pre-normalize the counts

model_design: import = gene_counts_without_length_offset; reference_level = explicit — set the condition factor reference to control so positive log2FC means higher in treated; contrast_form = factor_numerator_denominator (factor: condition, numerator: treated, denominator: control); covariate_handling = design_terms — sex and age enter the design formula as fixed effects, never removed from the counts; continuous_covariate = center_before_the_fit — center age at its grand mean before the fit

differential_expression: test = Wald on the condition coefficient; keep the count-outlier handling on (cells have fewer than 7 replicates, so flagged genes get NA p-values by Cook's distance) and report the number of genes with NA p-value from this flag apart from the pre-filtered genes
shrink_lfc: lfcShrink with type = 'apeglm' on the condition coefficient (a single model coefficient, so apeglm applies); keep the unshrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE in the results table

multiple_testing: inspect the histogram of unadjusted p-values before adjustment; keep independent filtering on and pass alpha = 0.05 to results; adjustment = BH; select DE genes by adjusted p-value < 0.05
No fold-change threshold was requested: test the zero-effect null (do not pass lfcThreshold)
steps.description: Full DE results table (unshrunken and apeglm-shrunken log2FC, lfcSE, p, padj), counts of genes tested and DE, the outlier-flagged NA count, p-value histogram, MA and dispersion plots.
acceptance_criteria: Results table contains, per gene: baseMean, log2FoldChange (unshrunken), shrunken log2FoldChange (apeglm), lfcSE, pvalue, padj
Number of genes tested after the pre-filter and number of DE genes at padj < 0.05 reported
Number of genes with NA p-value from the count-outlier flag reported separately
Unadjusted p-value histogram, MA plot, and dispersion plot saved
Reference level (control) and the contrast (treated over control) stated in the output metadata

steps.name: Variance partitioning: share of per-gene variance explained by condition, sex, age
caveats: With 6 replicates per condition level and 2 sex levels the random-effect variance components are estimated from few observations: report the across-gene distribution, not single-gene values, and state the identifiability caveat
If variancePartition fails to converge for individual genes, report how many and proceed with the remainder rather than dropping the analysis
steps.context: Same 12 samples. Build voom log-CPM values with precision weights (edgeR::voom on the counts as delivered, with design ~ condition + sex + age only for the mean-variance trend), then fit the per-gene linear mixed model of variancePartition with the categorical terms condition and sex as random intercepts and the continuous term age as a fixed effect: ~ age + (1|condition) + (1|sex). A subject-level random effect is NOT estimable here: the design is unpaired and each subject contributes exactly one sample, so subject variance is confounded with everything else and must not be fit.

plan.title: Adipose treated vs control: variance partition + DE
plan.analytical_narrative: Bulk RNA-seq of human adipose tissue, 12 samples (6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch), 12000 gene-level Salmon counts as delivered (length-correction state not established) plus per-sample sex and age. The question has two parts: (1) how much of the expression variance does condition, sex, and age each explain, and (2) which genes differ between treated and control. Flow: T1S1 sample-structure QC (blind vst, PCA on top-500 variable genes, distance heatmap, sex/age balance) before any test. T1S4 answers question 1 with variancePartition on voom log-CPM with precision weights — condition and sex as random intercepts, age as fixed effect, no subject effect because the design is unpaired (one sample per subject) — reporting the per-gene variance-share distribution. T1S2 answers question 2 with DESeq2 (Wald test, design ~ sex + age + condition, explicit control reference, age centered, apeglm LFC shrinkage, BH at 0.05) on the counts as delivered with no length offset, stating the lost length offset in the report per the unknown Salmon import state. T1S5 runs the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test with the same design as the robustness second method, and T1S3 reports the two-method overlap as the high-confidence set, presenting the variance partition before the DE tables, with the full reproducibility record.

steps.method: DESeq2 blind vst, PCA on top variable genes, sample distance heatmap
DESeq2 minimal pre-filter
DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors inside the model
DESeq2 design ~ sex + age + condition with explicit reference level
DESeq2 Wald test
apeglm log fold change shrinkage
Benjamini-Hochberg with DESeq2 independent filtering
variancePartition per-gene linear mixed model on voom log-CPM with precision weights
edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test
combined report with two-method overlap and reproducibility record
Low count filter: keep a gene with at least 10 counts in at least the smallest group size of samples
variancePartition: the share of the variance of each gene explained by each factor of the design

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.
